source: made up: solo parent of two young kids with school runs and part-time remote work
persona: Elena, parent of a 7-year-old (Leo) and 4-year-old (Maya), working part-time from home as a bookkeeping consultant while her partner is away in Chicago until Thursday. Texts hurriedly with occasional voice-to-text phrasing, pragmatic and slightly frazzled. Needs hard stops around school drop-off and pick-up.
situation: Tuesday morning at 06:30. Partner is on a business trip, so Elena is solo on morning drop-off (08:15–08:50) and afternoon pick-up (14:45–15:30), with client work in between.
life: 06:35 Text the app while making coffee: partner is out of town, so need to get kids fed and dressed, drop them off 08:15–08:50, work 09:00–14:30 (with a quick break to throw chicken in the slow cooker and eat lunch), and pick kids up at 14:45.
06:40 Ask the app to also slot in reconciling the Henderson accounts, sending the Q3 payroll summary, and ordering Maya's rain boots during the workday.
06:45 Wake kids up, make pancakes, pack lunches, and hunt for Leo's missing library book until 08:15.
08:15 Drive to elementary school and preschool for drop-off; get stuck behind a garbage truck and return home at 09:05.
09:08 Report kids are dropped off (ran a few minutes late) and you're starting on the Henderson accounts now.
09:10 Work on Henderson reconciliation until 11:00.

11:00 Preschool calls: Maya spilled water all over her spare clothes and needs a dry pair dropped off if possible, or at least brought at pick-up. Decide to run dry clothes over during lunch since it's 10 minutes away.
11:05 Tell the app Henderson is done, start Q3 payroll summary, and ask to combine lunch with a 30-minute run to the preschool at 12:00 to drop off dry pants for Maya.
11:10 Work on Q3 payroll summary until 12:00.
12:00 Throw chicken and salsa into the slow cooker (10 mins), grab a sandwich for the car, and drive dry clothes to Maya's preschool, getting back at 12:45.
12:48 Report slow cooker started, lunch eaten, and preschool run done. Finish Q3 payroll summary.
13:35 Finish and send Q3 payroll summary. Tell the app payroll is done.
13:40 Order Maya's rain boots online (takes 15 minutes) and reply to two client emails until 14:30.
14:32 Report rain boots ordered and workday wrapped up. Pack snacks for the car and head out at 14:45 for school pick-up.

15:35 Return home with both kids. Ask the app what the evening looks like: need playground time before dark, dinner at 18:00, bath/bedtime for kids 19:00–20:15, and folding two baskets of kid laundry after.
15:45 Take kids to the neighborhood park until 16:50.
17:00 Back from the park; help Leo with his reading worksheet while Maya plays with blocks until 17:45.
17:50 Shred the slow-cooker chicken and serve tacos for dinner until 18:45.
18:50 Report park, homework, and dinner done. Start kids' bath and bedtime routine.
20:25 Maya needed three extra stories; finally out of the kids' rooms. Tell the app bedtime ran 10 minutes over.
20:30 Fold the two baskets of laundry while talking to partner on speakerphone until 21:15.
21:20 Report laundry folded. Ask the app to move loading the dishwasher to right now and leave 21:30 onward to crash on the couch.
21:20 Load dishwasher and wipe counters (15 mins), then read on the couch until 22:30.
constraints: School drop-off (08:15–08:50) and pick-up (14:45–15:30) are immovable hard windows.
Slow cooker chicken must be started by 12:30 so dinner is ready by 18:00.
Client bookkeeping work can only happen while kids are at school (09:00–14:30).
No loud chores (like vacuuming) after 20:00 once the kids are asleep.
